name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise (5-Second Eccentric)
description: The 5-second eccentric lateral raise extends the lowering phase to a full 5 seconds, creating even greater time under tension for the medial deltoid than the 3-second version. It is an advanced hypertrophy technique and is typically used by experienced trainees for single set shock protocols or as a technique to maintain medial deltoid stimulus when heavy loads are unavailable or not advisable due to injury constraints.

execution.starting_position: Sit upright on a bench with dumbbells at the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a very light dumbbell — a 5-second eccentric with heavy weight is impossible to control. Many trainees use 2-5 kg.
steps: Step 1: Raise both arms to shoulder height in 1-2 seconds.
Step 2: Hold 1 second at the top.
Step 3: Lower both arms over exactly 5 seconds — one, two, three, four, five.
Step 4: Return to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale raising. Inhale controlled through the 5-second descent.
common_mistakes: Cheating the tempo — 5 seconds means 5 seconds
Using too heavy a weight — with 5s eccentric, light weight burns plenty
safety_considerations: Very light loads only — the extended time under tension is the stimulus, not the weight
High fatigue technique — limit to 1-2 sets initially
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder height to sides over 5 controlled seconds.
coaching_cues: Count every second of the descent
No shortcuts — the 5-second lower is the entire point
Fight the weight all the way to the bottom
